title: Call to Bind Ourselves to Christ
english: …My son, you have ascended.” And the nations were bound in Him unloosably. Therefore, we should also bind ourselves to Christ unloosably. If we strive at all to be saved and benefited from His feasts, He will raise us like Lazarus from our dead works, which were done without Him. So we dine with Him in Bethany, which is translated as the house of obedience, gathering our thoughts from the captivity of forgetfulness with the senses of the body, crying out and saying: “Hosanna in the highest; blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord” (Psalm 118:26), to enter into His Jerusalem, not to suffer as He did then, but to save it and be glorified by it.

As David says to Jerusalem: “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion” (Psalm 148:13). He said “praise” and “praise” with soul and body, “for He has strengthened the bars of your gates” (Psalm 147:13), which are faith, hope, and love.
translator_notes: The Greek text begins mid-sentence, so the translation starts with an ellipsis.
The text is a fragment; the translation is rendered literally as such.
